text: Why? Nobody knows for sure.
Historians suspect a mix.
Rivers changing course, a river drying up,
and the monsoon growing weaker for years.
People drifted east and south into smaller villages,
the drains filled with mud.
The cities were forgotten for almost 4,000 years.
But how did the world rediscover them?
through a railway. In the 1850s, British engineers were building a railway line in Punjab. They

bricks just lying in the ground. Sir, there's an old ruin full of bricks over there. Free
Bricks! Splendid! Oh, ruins never matter. Oh, they matter. They really, really matter.

But the land didn't stay empty for long. Over the mountains in the northwest, new people
were coming. They brought horses, chariots. And a collection of hymns so sacred, it was
passed down word for word by memory alone for more than 3,000 years.
Now this one, people still argue about.
